source.title: Identifying Generalization Properties in Neural Networks
source.authors: Huan Wang; N. Keskar; Caiming Xiong; R. Socher

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures train–test loss gaps across batch sizes and learning rates, and compares those gaps with a proposed Hessian-based generalization metric. This is a conceptual test of measured properties tracking the gap, using a different metric from V7.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports perturbed optimization results, but those compare its own proposed algorithm with standard optimizers; they do not measure a claim version's object as defined, so they are not rows. Batch-size and learning-rate figure results are described in text, but precise values are not stated.
record.test_reason: The batch-size experiments report test loss minus training loss, which can increase without held-out performance worsening as V5 requires. The pacGen score is a Hessian- and parameter-scale-based bound proxy, rather than V7's measured tolerance to magnitude-scaled perturbations before training error rises. Neither comparison directly tests a supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors derive PAC-Bayes bounds for perturbed models involving Hessian information, local Hessian smoothness, parameter scales and sample count. Their heuristic experiments show pacGen following loss-gap trends and a perturbation algorithm decreasing training accuracy while increasing test or validation accuracy. These bounds do not establish that sharpness alone determines an unperturbed model's generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a PAC-Bayes/Hessian-derived metric Ψ and heuristic sweeps of batch size and learning rate; V7 specifies magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness across networks and comparisons with other measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported gap and Ψ trends vary with batch size and learning rate; dataset is also varied between MNIST and CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: The test-minus-training loss gap tends to grow with batch size on MNIST and CIFAR-10 under fixed learning rates without learning-rate annealing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches can increase the train–test loss gap in these SGD experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch size 256, decreasing the learning rate increases the loss gap on MNIST, with similar trends reported on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate affects the train–test loss gap in these experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The approximate pacGen score follows the reported loss-gap trends across batch-size and learning-rate sweeps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A PAC-Bayes-inspired score combining approximate Hessian information, local smoothness and parameter scales qualitatively tracks loss gaps in the tested sweeps.

record.code_released: https://github.com/pytorch/examples/tree/master/mnist (the cited model example; paper code release not stated)
record.problems: The empirical sections are explicitly described as heuristic approximations, not rigorous. The MNIST and CIFAR-10 results are presented in plots without precise numerical values in the text; no uncertainty estimates or controls are reported. The text does not give the batch-size values or epoch budget needed to establish V5's fixed-epoch condition.
record.rows_left_out: Section 8, Figure 7 compares the authors' proposed perturbed optimizer with standard optimization methods; those are results for the paper's new method rather than direct measurements of the claim versions, so they are omitted under the row gate.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out accuracy in the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under comparable tuning; different optimizers on different datasets in Section 8 provide no such comparison.

Whether larger batches worsen held-out performance at matched epoch budgets, and whether adapted recipes remove that penalty. Figures 3–4 use epochs as their horizontal axis, but report loss differences rather than held-out loss or accuracy separately.
Dropout versus no-dropout comparisons and dependence on dropout strength or training-set size.
Measured magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with gaps among similarly fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any supplied version. Learning-rate dependence supplies no limits_scope verdict for V5. Section 8's optimizer comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out and do not compare Adam with SGD on a common workload. Numerical plot contents are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width increases past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD generalization under tuning.

Whether larger batches hurt under fixed epoch budgets across image classifiers and language models; adaptive recipes such as longer training, warmup, normalization, and regularization. The reported experiments vary batch size over epochs and use SGD without LR annealing heuristics.
Dropout's effect on test error across data regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures; correlational ranking across networks of one convolutional family.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: same model without dropout from the PyTorch example
rows.operation_detail: Measured test loss minus training loss and Ψγ,ε across epochs while varying batch size.
rows.measure: Test loss minus training loss; Ψγ=0.1,ε=0.1
rows.value: As batch size grows, the gap between test loss and training loss tends to get larger; Ψ shows the same trend. Precise values are figure only.
rows.note: Text explicitly describes the trend; no exact gap values or batch-size settings are given in the text.
rows.check: The reported increase in the loss gap is accurate, but does not establish higher test loss or error at matched epochs. Agreement between pacGen and the gap does not measure V7's perturbation tolerance. Separate the loss-gap and pacGen measures.

rows.subject: same model without dropout from the PyTorch example
rows.operation_detail: Measured test loss minus training loss and Ψγ,ε across epochs while varying learning rate at fixed batch size.
rows.measure: Test loss minus training loss; Ψγ=0.1,ε=0.1
rows.value: As learning rate decreases, the gap between test loss and training loss increases; Ψ shows a similar trend. Precise values are figure only.
rows.note: Supports a relation between the measured metric and gap, but this is a learning-rate sweep, not the large-batch condition in V5.
rows.check: A learning-rate sweep at fixed batch size does not test V5. The pacGen trend does not measure V7's perturbation tolerance; 'partial' incorrectly treats a different measure as incomplete evidence for the version. Separate the two measures.
